# [TASK] Add /work-issue skill — interactive per-issue work-loop automation

## Task
Add a repo-local skill (`.claude/skills/work-issue/`) that runs one GitHub
issue through CLAUDE.md's implement → test → review → close work loop
interactively, for a human-driven session rather than the scheduled
`lmdb-autonomous-dev` routine.

## No parent
Pure process/tooling work, no user-facing slice. No parent Story.

## Scope
The skill itself only (a Markdown instruction file), not a change to
CLAUDE.md's actual contract — process-improvement findings surfaced while
building/using it are reported for the user to decide on, not applied
unilaterally.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `/work-issue` (or `/work-issue <N>`) runs picking → implementation →
      module tests/lint/coverage → two independent review passes (code +
      test-quality) → issue-hygiene resync/close → commit/push, matching
      CLAUDE.md's per-issue loop
- [x] Skips the `.autonomous-lock`/`.autonomous-halt` coordination (that
      exists for concurrent scheduled checkouts, not a live session) while
      still honoring an in-flight `WIP:` commit and the 2+ `WIP:` stuck-task
      rule
- [x] Corrects one real picking-order gap found by using it for real: reads
      a parent Story's own "Technical Tasks" list order before falling
      back to priority-label sorting (`.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md`,
      "1. Pick the issue" step 4)
- [x] Captures concrete, evidence-based process-improvement suggestions
      surfaced while dogfooding it (not speculative ones) for the user to
      decide on, rather than silently changing `CLAUDE.md` itself
      (`.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md`, "Suggested process
      improvements" section, 4 items)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 2

## Notes
Written and dogfooded in the same session against #202 — the skill's
picking/loop/hygiene steps are exactly what was run to take #202 from pick
to close, not a theoretical process written and left unexercised.

Audited by #317: the "## No parent" reason was written inside an HTML
comment, invisible on GitHub's rendered page. Replaced with plain text.
